en-US.author: InstaZDLL
en-US.description: Local-first music player with Hi-Res audio, AutoMix, word-synced lyrics, smart playlists, themes and plugins. No account or subscription.
en-US.longDescription:
WaveFlow is a local-first music player for Windows, macOS and Linux. It scans your music folders, organizes everything by album, artist and genre, and plays it through its own real-time audio engine. No account, no subscription, no streaming service: your music stays on your machine.

It plays Hi-Res files, DSD and 5.1 / 7.1 on the speakers they name, with gapless playback, crossfades and AutoMix on the beat, ReplayGain, an equalizer and exclusive output. It adds lyrics synced word by word with a lyrics editor, smart playlists, Daily Mix and Release Radar, a tag workshop and MusicBrainz enrichment with undo, WebDAV and SMB shares, podcasts, six skins and fourteen themes, Last.fm and ListenBrainz, DLNA and MPD servers, and sandboxed plugins, in 17 languages.
en-US.name: WaveFlow
en-US.releaseNotes:
2.0.1 (2026-11-10)
🩹 What's new in v2.0.1
Warning
The builds are still being made. The downloads below should be in place within the hour, and the in-app updater offers 2.0.1 from then on. AUR, COPR and APT follow right after; winget waits for its review at Microsoft, which can take a day or two.
Important
Coming from 1.9? Read the WaveFlow 2.0.0 notes first: they present the new interface and everything else 2.0 brings, and explain that your library is upgraded the first time 2.0 opens it, after a verified backup — 1.9 cannot open it afterwards.
The first fixes after 2.0: a track whose file is gone now says so, the Liked tracks count follows your hearts, switching profiles brings up the new profile's music right away, and an empty cover picture no longer hides the real one.
🎧 Playback
- A missing file says so when you start it. Double-clicking a track whose file was deleted outside WaveFlow, or starting an album or a playlist on it, showed that track as playing while the previous one carried on, with no message, and Play then went back to the previous track. It now behaves as it already did when the queue reached such a file: the previous track stops, the player stays on the missing one and the "This track could not be played" alert appears. A track on a network share that does not answer shows its own message. The track is not marked as missing, since an unplugged drive is not a deleted file: the next scan decides. (#1068, refs #1065)
💚 Liked tracks and profiles
- The Liked tracks count follows your hearts. The count in the sidebar and on Home did not move when you liked or unliked a track, so it could stay stale until something else refreshed it, often the next launch. It now changes as soon as you like or unlike a track, in every skin, and after a scan or a duplicate sent to the trash. A like copied from your WaveFlow Server updates it too. (#1069, refs #1066)
- Switching profiles shows the new profile's music. The open page stayed on the previous profile: Liked tracks kept its list until you left and came back, and an open album could even show an album of the other profile. A switch now reloads the page and the search bar and starts a fresh history. An album, artist, genre or playlist that was open takes you to the matching tab of the library, since it belongs to the other profile, and the page starts at the top. (#1069, refs #1067)
🖼️ Covers
- An empty front cover no longer hides the real one. A file whose tags began with an empty front cover picture got no cover at all, even with a valid picture behind it. WaveFlow now takes the first picture that holds an image. A file already in your library is read again only when it changes, so for one that showed no cover, use Deep rescan on its folder. (#1072, refs #1071)
📦 Recommended install
Use your platform's package manager when one is available, so updates keep flowing through the tool you already use.
Windows
winget install InstaZDLL.WaveFlow
Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS / CachyOS
yay -S waveflow-bin
# or: paru -S waveflow-bin
Fedora / RHEL / Rocky / Alma / CentOS Stream
sudo dnf copr enable instazdll/waveflow
sudo dnf install waveflow
Debian / Ubuntu / Mint / Pop!_OS
The Debian package is wave-flow (kebab-case, required by the Debian naming spec — Tauri bundles it that way from the WaveFlow product name).
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://packages.buildkite.com/instazdll/waveflow/gpgkey \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/waveflow.gpg
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/waveflow.gpg] https://packages.buildkite.com/instazdll/waveflow/any/ any main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/waveflow.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install wave-flow
macOS
curl -fsSL https://waveflow.app/install.sh | bash
WaveFlow is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS refuses to open a copy downloaded by a browser. The script removes the quarantine flag from WaveFlow.app only and changes no system setting; --help lists its options. It is scripts/install-macos.sh, to read before running it. The .dmg below works too: right-click → Open the first time, or run xattr -cr /Applications/WaveFlow.app.
Standalone download
Everything is also available as a raw bundle below — .AppImage, .deb, .rpm, .exe, .msi, .dmg.
🐛 If something goes wrong
Open an issue with your OS, the exact steps, and your logs — Settings → Maintenance → Diagnostics → Copy logs puts them on your clipboard, ready to paste.
Thanks to @GoEverLo for three precise reports, and keep the feedback coming. 💚
Full changelog: v2.0.0...v2.0.1
